threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think 'the tube' can get you anywhere. The bus routes here are the real lifeline, mate.
Caught a woman singing to herself on the 196. She was convinced it was a private concert—everyone else just pretended not to notice.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: One afternoon I saw a neighbor watering their plants while their cat lazily watched a pigeon steal a croissant from the doorstep. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, you can buy a currywurst from a stand while a techno DJ spins records right beside you—only in Berlin can street food and nightlife collide like this.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they instinctively dodge the skateboarders on Valencia while holding a taco, like it’s an Olympic sport.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full suit dance on the 47 like it was his personal stage this morning. Only in SF do we mix commuting with Broadway.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the Plaza, but the real charm is in the hidden alleys where locals gather for sunny vermut on a Tuesday.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by the way they fumble with the T-10 card at the metro, as if it’s a rare treasure instead of a simple transit pass.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused when the bus driver asks for exact change; everyone else just pulls out cash without a second thought.
Last night on the 59, I overheard a couple arguing about an ex they hadn’t seen in years. So detailed, it felt like watching a soap opera unfold.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy in a tutu juggling flaming torches outside the Kiosk on Hermannplatz at 2 AM. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You know you're in Kreuzberg when late-night kebab shops play 90s Turkish pop, and it's as normal as a beer garden on a sunny day.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they know to skip BART on Friday evenings—nothing like overheated brakes and a smoke scare to ruin plans.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni driver busting out an impromptu dance between stops. The passengers loved it—guess the delays bring out the life!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just hop on any tram, but those of us living here know the 3 is a rare sight after 10 PM. Missing it means a long walk or more waiting.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re still clutching that oversized map while trying to navigate the metro. You can spot them pausing at every corner, looking befuddled.
